text: The King-Spadina area has grown rapidly in recent decades. Between 1996 and 2018, the population increased from just 945 residents to approximately 22,000 residents, and local employment increased from 21,000 jobs to about 46,000 jobs. There is a great deal of additional development approved or proposed in King-Spadina, with the potential to add another 30,000 residents in the coming years. The section of Wellington Street West between Spadina Avenue and Portland Street, "Wellington Place," is unique in Toronto. Plans for a broad, tree-lined avenue linking Clarence Square Park and Victoria Memorial Square Park were in the original plans for the development of the area when it first transitioned from being the Military Reserve. City Council direct the Deputy City Manager, Infrastructure and Development Services to coordinate the implementation of construction projects in the vicinity of Wellington Street West and Draper Street, including: a. the north boulevard of Wellington Street West between Clarence Square Park and Victoria Memorial Square Park; b. the full reconstruction and redesign of Draper Street; c. planned cycling infrastructure; d. water main replacement; and e. the design of the new City park at 456 Wellington Street West. 2.
